name: Supramid implant

card.summary: A nylon (polyamide) mesh used as a facial implant material, historically for chin and nasal augmentation to build out facial contour.
card.note: Reviews describe resorption and foreign-body reactions; newer implant materials are more commonly used today.

quick.overview:
Supramid is a brand of nylon polyamide mesh made by S. Jackson, Inc. that surgeons have used as an alloplastic (synthetic) implant to add projection to the chin and the nasal dorsum. A mesh implant is shaped by the surgeon and placed over bone to enhance facial contour.

Surgical reviews from the 1980s and 1990s list it among implant options alongside Gore-Tex, Medpor, Silastic and Mersilene, and report that it tends to resorb over time. It is also used in other fields, for example as a suture and in eyelid ptosis repair.
quick.how: A surgeon sculpts the mesh to the planned shape and places it in a pocket over the chin or nasal bone through an incision. Surgeons choose between autogenous tissue (the patient's own cartilage or bone) and alloplastic materials like this one based on the site and personal preference.
quick.risks: Reviews report that the polyamide mesh can provoke a foreign-body reaction and gradually resorb, which may reduce the augmentation over time. Reported complications of facial alloplasts generally include infection, extrusion and displacement. It is a surgical device; decisions belong with a qualified facial plastic surgeon.

lead: Supramid is a polyamide (nylon) material sold by S. Jackson, Inc. of Virginia as sutures and as sterile mesh sheets and shaped implants for plastic and reconstructive surgery. In facial surgery it was used as an alloplastic implant for chin (mentoplasty) and nasal augmentation, adding projection that changes the facial profile.

A 2000 review of chin augmentation lists Supramid among synthetic implant options, with Gore-Tex, Medpor, Silastic and Mersilene, and observes that no one implant is perfect for every face [1]. A 1995 review of nasal implants states that some authors tried Supramid mesh, which tends to resorb, while Mersilene seemed to resist resorption [2].
Within looksmaxxing and hardmaxxing discussions it appears as one of the materials in the history of facial implants rather than as a current favourite.

chain: Mesh is shaped by the surgeon
Placed over chin or nasal bone
angle.text: An implant adds volume where bone is receded, which can improve profile balance for the chin or nasal bridge. Because the material is reported to resorb, the volume added may decrease over time.

paras: Supramid is a nylon polyamide. In ophthalmic plastic surgery, a polyfilament Supramid suture has been used as the suspensory material in frontalis suspension for congenital ptosis, and recent reviews continue to list it among options with silicone rod, Gore-Tex and Mersilene [3]. The same name appears in tendon repair, skin closure and glaucoma shunt stenting literature.

For augmentation, a 1987 materials-selection review notes that choosing a graft depends on the material (density, sculptability, tissue reaction, resorption, migration, infection, extrusion and ease of removal) and the site, and that resorption is a potential problem with all biologic grafts and possibly with Supramid [4].

A 1990 canine study compared Proplast, high-density polyethylene (Medpor), silicone rubber (Silastic), polyamide mesh (Supramid) and rib bone for facial bone augmentation, assessing gross behaviour and tissue response [5]. The 1995 nasal implant review states that autogenous tissue remained the authors' preferred method for augmenting the nasal dorsum, and describes Silicone as having fallen out of favour [2].

No modern randomized trials of Supramid for cosmetic facial augmentation were found. Published work consists of narrative reviews [1][2][4], an animal comparison of facial implant materials [5], and ophthalmic series: a Wills Eye Hospital review of 145 frontalis suspension procedures compared Supramid Extra cable-type suture with fascia lata and reported failures in 40.5 percent of the Supramid procedures from ptosis recurrence or granuloma formation [7].

timeline.event: Comparative animal study of facial augmentation materials including polyamide mesh [5].
